title: flex-basis applies to the PARENT's main axis — % basis on a column parent overrides height, not width
trigger: Setting flex:<grow> <shrink> <basis> on an element whose parent may be flex-direction:column — the basis then applies to HEIGHT and silently overrides the height property
principle: flex-basis always resolves along the flex parent's MAIN axis. On a flex-row parent it sets width; on a flex-column parent it sets height — and a non-auto flex-basis WINS over the height/width property. A wrapper styled 'flex:1 1 100%; height:389px' inside a column parent collapses to content height (the % basis resolves against an indefinite container height → falls back to content). Fix pattern: only apply a width-intended basis when the insert parent is verified flex-row; non-row parents get flex:0 0 auto (basis auto → the height property governs; on non-flex parents flex is inert anyway).

cases.context: Split View wrapper inserted into StreamFlix .playerSection (display:flex; flex-direction:column). wrapper cssText 'flex:1 1 100%; height:389px' → basis 100% applies to height axis, container height indefinite → resolves to content height → wrapper 49px (panel header only), stageTihoka+video 0px — video disappears.

Same fix site, sibling symptom: wrapper height was set to parentPixelHeight for all parents — correct only for flex-row parents whose height is sibling-stretch-driven (kisskh .row taller than the video col). On column/block parents the parent height contains unrelated page content → panel towers over the page.
cases.bad: height:`${Math.round(parentPixelHeight)}px` // all parents → 2500px wrapper on a content column
cases.good: height: isRowParent ? parentPx : playerShellPx // row: fill stretched Tihoka; else match the player's own box

applyFor: Content-script wrappers/portals inserted into arbitrary host-page parents (unknown display/flex-direction)
Any element given a width-intended flex-basis that may land inside a column-flex container
Split View / docked panel / side-by-side layouts that reparent host elements into a flex row
